title: Search Engine Autocomplete
short_description: Engineer high-throughput search query suggestion systems using trie indexers, prefix lookups, and token analyzers.
real_world_context: Web search engines and real-time social search bars process tens of billions of keystrokes each day. Every time a user types a letter, the autocomplete backend must match prefix queries in sub-millisecond response windows, compress query URL navigation breadcrumbs, and dissect search phrases into unique substring tokens for query intent classification and search ad targeting.
learning_objectives: Implement an in-memory prefix tree (Trie) supporting rapid query insertion and exact match lookups.
Query prefix subtrees to retrieve lexicographically ordered autocomplete suggestions.
Analyze URL paths and routing keys to determine the Longest Common Prefix (LCP) for query compression.
Count distinct query sub-tokens to evaluate search intent entropy using substring analysis.
